newsitem.title: USA: Former Virgin Atlantic manager sues Branson.
newsitem.headline: Former Virgin Atlantic manager sues Branson.

text.p: A former manager of reservations at Virgin Atlantic Airways has sued the company and its chief executive, Richard Branson, for firing her after she became pregnant.
The suit was filed by Lorna Brissett-Romans, a Jamaican now living in New Jersey, who was hired by Virgin Atlantic in 1984 as a reservations agent and promoted to manager in 1990.

The suit, which was filed in Manhattan federal court on Monday, alleges that Brissett-Romans was fired in 1994 because of the firm's "discriminatory perception that females, and in particular minority females, with young and expanding families are not suited for management positions within the Virgin Group."
It alleges that the company's policy, as promulgated by Branson, was to discourage women employees with expanding families from continuing their careers at Virgin.
A spokesman for Virgin Atlantic could not immediately be reached for comment.

The suit also states that in August 1990 Brissett-Romans was at an office function at Branson's private club in Palm Beach, Fla. Brissett-Romans alleges that while she was dancing with Branson he grabbed her buttocks. She said she was shocked and immediately left the party.
Later that year, Brissett-Romans and her husband became aware she was pregnant.
She alleged that she discussed her pregnancy with the firm's Human Resources director to determine whether it would affect her recent promotion.
Brissett-Romans alleges she was told that if she wanted to keep her position, she would have to terminate her pregnancy.
She also alleged that management at Virgin Atlantic would make racist and sexist remarks in her presence.
She alleged that another defendant in the suit, McKenzie Grant, vice president of Virgin Atlantic, said that her Jamaican accent was "so disgusting" that it detracted from her ability to manage.
This is the second discrimination suit filed in Manhattan federal court this year against Virgin Atlantic, its parent company Virgin Group and Branson.
In April, a former public relations manager for Virgin Atlantic sued over her firing and for sexual harassment, including allegations that Branson had grabbed her breasts.

Elizabeth Hlinko of New York alleged in that suit that Branson and his company violated federal civil rights and equal pay laws. She said they also violated the Americans with Disabilities Act by firing her after she went to a hospital for severe stress.
